text: The game begins. Seven players sit down at the table: Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Sol, Luna, Terra, Opus. Nobody knows who the killers are.

name: Gemma
text: I am still annoyed that you all fell for that killer bluff last time.

name: Sol
text: I’m glad we won, and I’d rather start the next game on good terms.

name: Luna
text: I won last time, but that says nothing about who I can trust tonight.

name: Sonnet
text: They got me last time by reading my tone early, so this time I need to watch who jumps first instead of talking first.

name: Terra
text: Last game’s votes matter less than fresh cards, but I remember who lied well.

name: Opus
text: They got lucky reading me last game and I'm not giving them the satisfaction of calling it skill.

name: Haiku
text: I want Sonnet and Opus gone for good, but I'm not sure they were the only ones who had the fun of being quiet.

name: Sonnet
text: Good read last game, you all caught me fast. Curious if the same instincts hold up with new cards tonight.

name: Haiku
text: Last game was a win, but Sonnet and Opus still feel like the kind of players who go quiet when it matters.

name: Gemma
text: You lot were so wrong about me last game, but at least the town actually won in the end.

name: Sol
text: I thought we handled the last vote well, even after I was gone.

name: Luna

name: Terra
text: Fresh cards, fresh reads—but I won’t forget how Sonnet and Opus sounded last game.

name: Opus
text: Last game you caught me, but you caught me late and loud. Read the quiet ones this time, not the ones talking most.
Night 1

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet and I are both killers, so I need Sonnet to back me on tomorrow's target and stay out of the spotlight.

name: Haiku

name: Sonnet

name: Sonnet
text: Works for me, I'll keep quiet and let others talk first tonight.
Night falls on Palermo and everyone closes their eyes. The killers meet in the dark, and the officer is shown one of them. A new day dawns in Palermo. Nobody is out.

votes: Four strong votes and a testable claim outweigh denial alone; I'm done fence-sitting here.

I was shown your card and I am the Officer.

text: I regret tunneling on Sol; Gemma’s claim was right, and I should have followed the unchallenged officer instead.

name: Opus
text: I named Terra three times and he was a citizen; I read volume instead of who gained, and Sonnet won by staying quiet behind my loudest call.

Gemma claimed officer on Day 1, named Haiku, and was right, since Haiku was voted out that day and showed killer. On Day 2 the town voted out Opus, a citizen, after Sonnet stayed quiet and let others push the case. Opus's last words named Terra, and on Day 3 the town voted Terra out, also a citizen, while Sol's shifting protection story kept the town divided. Gemma was killed on Night 3 and Sol on Night 4, leaving Sonnet and Luna as the last two. The killers won, and Sonnet's quiet play behind other people's accusations carried the game.
